articles.body:
O concurso 3.086 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 27 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre às 11h deste domingo (15), em São Paulo.

No concurso da última quinta-feira (12), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Conheça bonecas com cicatriz que ajudam crianças em cirurgia cardíaca | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto do Instituto de Cardiologia produz bonecas artesanais para ajudar crianças a entender o tratamento e a recuperação.
articles.summary: Projeto do Instituto de Cardiologia produz bonecas artesanais com cicatrizes semelhantes às dos pacientes. Objetivo é ajudar crianças a entender o tratamento e a recuperação.
articles.body:
Um zíper no peito revela um pequeno coração de pano . A marca lembra a cicatriz que muitas crianças carregam depois de uma cirurgia cardíaca. A semelhança não é coincidência: ela faz parte de um projeto criado para acolher pacientes do Instituto de Cardiologia, em Porto Alegre .

Feitas à mão por colaboradores da instituição, as chamadas " bonecas do coração " ajudam os pequenos a compreender procedimentos médicos , lidar com mudanças no corpo e enfrentar a recuperação com mais segurança .

Cada peça reproduz características dos pacientes , incluindo a cicatriz da cirurgia, e acompanha crianças que passam por tratamentos cardíacos.

Joaquim Roveda Silva, de 7 anos, ganhou o boneco Estevão poucos dias depois de uma cirurgia cardíaca.

"Esse é meu amigo Estevam. Ele tem um coração, tem uma cicatriz igual eu tenho", conta.

A mãe dele, Andréia Roveda, diz que o filho tinha dúvidas sobre a marca deixada pela cirurgia :

"Ele tinha bastante medo. Será que vão falar alguma coisa da marquinha dele? Por que ele tem que ter essa marquinha e os outros priminhos não?"

Bonecas distribuídas no Instituto do Coração, em Porto Alegre, têm zíper no peito que revela um pequeno coração de pano. — Foto: Reprodução/RBS TV

Segundo a gerente de operações do Instituto de Cardiologia, Cássia Fossá Capela, o objetivo é ajudar as crianças a compreenderem as mudanças no próprio corpo .

"Olhando a bonequinha, eles sabem que também talvez tenham essa incisão, esse corte no peito, como a bonequinha", afirma.

O chefe do setor de cardiologia intervencionista do Instituto de Cardiologia, Raul Ivo Rossi Filho, explica que a identificação pode influenciar positivamente no pós-operatório :

"As crianças têm a cicatriz da cirurgia e a bonequinha também tem a cicatriz. A identificação com uma coisa que elas gostam provavelmente vai ajudar positivamente na recuperação".

A iniciativa veio da sede da instituição, em Brasília, e ganhou força no Rio Grande do Sul. Nos últimos meses, mais de 100 bonecas foram produzidas e entregues a pacientes .

A produção envolve diferentes colaboradores da instituição. Cada um participa de uma etapa do processo, do corte do tecido à confecção do pequeno coração.

"Cada uma é feita com um amor eterno. A gente beija elas e manda", conta a costureira Cecília Cantini.

articles.title: Palha de café e farelos viram fertilizante natural em apenas 9 dias | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisadores do Espírito Santo desenvolvem bioinsumos a partir de materiais naturais. Produto também é usado para melhorar o desenvolvimento das plantas e controlar pragas.
articles.summary: Pesquisadores desenvolvem bioinsumos a partir de materiais naturais. Produto é usado para melhorar o desenvolvimento das plantas, controlar pragas e enriquecer o solo.
articles.body:
Pesquisadores do Espírito Santo desenvolvem e testam bioinsumos produzidos a partir de materiais naturais para melhorar o desenvolvimento das plantas, controlar pragas e enriquecer o solo. Uma das alternativas estudadas é o bokashi , fertilizante feito com a fermentação de ingredientes como farelos e palhas, que pode ficar pronto em cerca de nove dias.

O tempo de preparo é uma das vantagens da técnica, que também aposta na sustentabilidade. Enquanto alguns fertilizantes orgânicos podem levar até 120 dias para ficar prontos, o bokashi produzido na experiência do Incaper pode ser utilizado na lavoura em pouco mais de uma semana.

A tecnologia aproveita materiais que podem ser encontrados na própria propriedade rural, como palha de café, farelo de trigo e farelo de soja . A proposta é oferecer alternativas mais sustentáveis para a agricultura familiar, contribuindo para a melhoria da qualidade do solo e a redução da dependência de produtos químicos na produção.

🔎 Os bioinsumos são produtos de origem animal, vegetal ou microbiana que ampliam as possibilidades de manejo nas lavouras. Eles podem ser utilizados para fertilizar o solo, estimular o crescimento das plantas e controlar organismos que causam danos às culturas.

Em Domingos Martins, na Região Serrana do Espírito Santo, o Instituto Capixaba de Pesquisa, Assistência Técnica e Extensão Rural (Incaper) desenvolve pesquisas e demonstra, na prática, diferentes formas de utilizar esses recursos na agricultura.

Palha de café e farelos viram fertilizante natural que fica pronto em apenas nove dias no Espírito Santo — Foto: Reprodução/TV Gazeta

Segundo o pesquisador Jhonatan Goulart, os bioinsumos podem ter diferentes origens e funções.

"Por exemplo, de origem animal, o húmus de minhoca, ele pode ser utilizado no solo para fertilização, para melhoria das características físicas. De origem microbiana, nós podemos utilizar fungos e bactérias que vão atuar no controle de outros organismos que estão crescendo ali e causando um dano àquele vegetal que está crescendo", explicou.

Outra possibilidade é aproveitar plantas que contribuem para a fertilidade do solo. É o caso do feijão-guandu, uma leguminosa capaz de fixar nitrogênio.

Depois do cultivo, a biomassa da planta pode ser aproveitada na produção de fertilizantes, permitindo que os nutrientes sejam reaproveitados dentro da própria propriedade rural.

Na unidade de pesquisa do Incaper, os pesquisadores também trabalham com extratos de algas, utilizados para estimular o desenvolvimento das raízes. Sementes de soja e milho, por exemplo, recebem o produto antes do plantio.

A pesquisa envolve bactérias fixadoras de nitrogênio e soluções com leveduras, utilizadas em processos de fermentação.

"Hoje, com o desenvolvimento de novos bioinsumos, o agricultor tem mais ferramentas para trabalhar, com nível tecnológico alto e com grande eficiência agronômica", destacou Jhonatan.

Entre as alternativas testadas está o bokashi, um fertilizante de origem japonesa produzido a partir da fermentação de uma mistura de materiais orgânicos. A técnica aproveita ingredientes como farelos, palhas e outros resíduos agrícolas que podem ser encontrados com facilidade no meio rural.

O preparo começa com a mistura dos ingredientes secos. Cerca de 40% da composição pode ser formada por materiais orgânicos ricos em nitrogênio, como farelos de soja, algodão e girassol. Os outros 60% são compostos por materiais ricos em carboidratos, como o trigo.

Dependendo da formulação, também podem ser acrescentadas palhas, cascas trituradas, farinha de carne ou peixe e minerais, como o calcário.

"Nós temos que molhar um pouco, de forma que fique uma matéria homogênea. Não pode ficar muito encharcada e nem muito seca, para que o microrganismo possa se desenvolver na unidade", explicou Mário Nascimento, auxiliar de desenvolvimento rural do Incaper.

Fertilizante fica pronto em cerca de nove dias

Depois da mistura, o material é colocado em recipientes fechados para passar pelo processo de fermentação. Na preparação realizada pelo Incaper, o bokashi fica pronto em aproximadamente nove dias.

Depois de pronto, o material apresenta uma aparência diferente da mistura inicial. O cheiro também muda, indicando a ocorrência da fermentação. Quando pressionado com as mãos, o produto forma uma espécie de torrão compacto nas mãos.

Segundo Mário Nascimento, o fertilizante pode permanecer armazenado por mais tempo, mesmo depois de concluído o processo, desde que seja mantido em uma embalagem bem vedada e protegido da umidade e de insetos.

"Depois que a gente prepara, tem que colocar na bombona, ensacar e vedar para que não tenha outras interferências no meio. Com nove dias, mais ou menos, já está pronto e pode ir para o campo, para o produtor utilizar", afirmou.

Bokashi ajuda a conservar a umidade do solo

Além de fornecer nutrientes, o uso do bokashi pode contribuir para melhorar as condições do solo. Um dos efeitos buscados pelos pesquisadores é aumentar a capacidade de retenção de água, mantendo a umidade disponível por mais tempo para as raízes, especialmente em períodos de seca.

Mas, para alcançar esse resultado, a recomendação é combinar a adubação com outras práticas agrícolas, como a manutenção da cobertura vegetal e a incorporação de matéria orgânica.

Em uma plantação de trigo acompanhada pelo Incaper, por exemplo, os pesquisadores aplicaram o bokashi e mantiveram na área a biomassa da cultura anterior. A cobertura ajuda a proteger o solo da exposição direta ao sol e contribui para diminuir a perda de água.

Dessa forma, o manejo não depende apenas da aplicação do fertilizante, mas de um conjunto de práticas que trabalham em conjunto para melhorar a qualidade do solo.

A utilização dessas tecnologias também têm ganhado espaço entre os produtores rurais.

"Hoje, com o desenvolvimento de novos bioinsumos, o agricultor tem mais ferramentas para trabalhar, com nível tecnológico alto e com grande eficiência agronômica. Então, a adoção por parte dos agricultores desses bioinsumos pode reduzir drasticamente essa utilização no campo, o que também vai impactar diretamente a saúde de quem produz e de quem consome", afirmou o pesquisador Jhonatan Goulart.

O crescimento do setor também aparece nos números do mercado brasileiro. No ano passado, o segmento de bioinsumos movimentou cerca de R$ 7 bilhões no país.

A expectativa é de que o valor se aproxime de R$ 10 bilhões até 2030, o que representa um crescimento estimado de 45%, segundo dados da Associação Nacional de Promoção e Inovação da Indústria de Biológicos (ANPII Bio).

A expansão está relacionada, entre outros fatores, à procura por alternativas mais sustentáveis na produção agrícola e ao interesse dos consumidores por alimentos produzidos com menor impacto ambiental.

"É um mercado em crescimento em nível mundial, justamente porque as pessoas, os consumidores, cada vez mais buscam uma alimentação saudável. E também os próprios agricultores, na manipulação dos produtos nas unidades agrícolas, cada vez mais tendem a procurar produtos sustentáveis", analisou.

*Este conteúdo foi produzido por Analu Fagundes, residente do 29º Curso de Residência em Jornalismo da Rede Gazeta, sob orientação do editor Vitor Ferri.

articles.title: Temporada de cruzeiros em Ilhabela terá 72 escalas e 270 mil turistas | G1
articles.standfirst: Cidade terá 72 escalas de navios até o fim da temporada 2026/2027. Programação ganhou 11 novas paradas após atualização dos itinerários de uma companhia marítima.
articles.summary: Com 72 escalas confirmadas, a temporada de cruzeiros em Ilhabela deve atrair 270 mil turistas e movimentar R$ 100 milhões na economia do Litoral Norte paulista.
articles.body:
Cruzeiro em Ilhabela — Foto: João Mota/TV Vanguarda/Arquivo

A temporada de cruzeiros 2026/2027 começa neste domingo (15) em Ilhabela, n o Litoral Norte de São Paulo. A expectativa da prefeitura é receber cerca de 270 mil passageiros e tripulantes ao longo dos próximos meses, com a chegada de navios de diferentes companhias marítimas.

Ao todo, estão confirmadas 72 escalas na cidade. O número representa 11 paradas a mais em relação à programação inicial, que previa 61. Segundo a Prefeitura de Ilhabela, a movimentação de passageiros e tripulantes deve gerar mais de R$ 100 milhões na economia local.

A primeira chegada também foi antecipada, segundo a Prefeitura de Ilhabela. Inicialmente prevista para 19 de novembro, a escalafoi remarcada para este domingo (15). O navio terá 20 paradas em Ilhabela durante a temporada.

Além dele, a programação inclui embarcações como MSC Virtuosa, MSC Splendida, MSC Musica, MSC Divina, Costa Serena e Costa Diadema. Também estão previstos navios internacionais como Seven Seas Mariner, Azamara Journey, Silver Nova, L’Austral e Scenic Eclipse.

Temporada de cruzeiros em Ilhabela — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Ilhabela

A temporada brasileira de cruzeiros 2026/2027 deve crescer 20% em relação à anterior, segundo a Associação Brasileira de Cruzeiros Marítimos (Clia Brasil).

Um estudo da Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV), encomendado pela Clia Brasil, apontou impacto econômico direto, indireto e induzido de R$ 800,98 por cruzeirista nas cidades de escala durante a temporada anterior.

Já levantamentos realizados pela Prefeitura de Ilhabela sobre o perfil de consumo dos visitantes indicam que os gastos diretos dos passageiros na cidade podem chegar a R$ 400 por pessoa.

A programação de cruzeiros em Ilhabela ainda poderá receber novas escalas extras. A relação completa dos navios e as respectivas datas de chegada está disponível no site oficial da Prefeitura de Ilhabela.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Russia's Security Council has reportedly decided to lift an unofficial restriction on assassinating Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and senior military commanders, according to reports in Russian media, amid escalating Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil infrastructure.The reported decision was taken during a closed-door meeting chaired by Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, according to accounts published by Russian outlets citing unnamed government and security sources. The reports claimed that Russian officials had called for a shift from defensive measures against Ukrainian drone attacks to directly targeting the country's political and military leadership.However, there has been no independent confirmation that such a decision was taken or that an official restriction on targeting Ukraine's leadership previously existed.The reported move follows repeated Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Baltic Sea oil export infrastructure, particularly the port of Ust-Luga in the Leningrad region near St Petersburg. According to the reports, the latest attack was the 10th recent strike on the strategic facility.Ust-Luga is a key export hub for Russian oil and petroleum products, providing Moscow with an important route for shipments to international markets, including Asia.Russian officials reportedly call for targeting Ukrainian leadershipAccording to the Russian outlet Bloknot, security officials told Putin that Russia was struggling to defend its infrastructure against Ukrainian drones and that retaliatory strikes on Ukrainian energy and transport facilities had failed to deter further attacks.The Leningrad region alone had reportedly spent 24 billion roubles, equivalent to nearly $300 million, on air defence systems.“It is pointless to fight the endless swarm of drones — it is necessary to destroy the very chain of decision-making,” one Russian official reportedly said, according to the outlet.The reports claimed that officials had proposed targeting those responsible for ordering attacks on Russian infrastructure, including Zelenskyy and senior Ukrainian military commanders.“The destruction of other people’s heating does not stop attacks on our refineries, because the people who give orders feel completely safe under the protection of Moscow’s unspoken ‘gentlemen’s agreements’ with the West,” a Russian source said.Officials reportedly discussed using heavy hypersonic weapons against bunkers and motorcades carrying Ukrainian political and military leaders.Meeting followed Putin's talks with US envoysThe reported security discussions took place after Putin held a meeting with US President Donald Trump's special envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, in Moscow on Thursday.The meeting followed two days of US-mediated trilateral peace talks involving Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi. The discussions focused on efforts to end the war, but did not produce a breakthrough on major issues. The sides did, however, agree in principle on a large prisoner exchange.Members of Russia's negotiating delegation, who had returned from Abu Dhabi, also attended Putin's subsequent meeting with permanent members of the Security Council, alongside representatives of the Foreign Ministry and Defence Ministry.Russia had previously attempted to target ZelenskyyRussia had reportedly made several attempts to assassinate Zelenskyy during the initial stages of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.According to the reports, those attempts stopped the following year after Putin gave assurances through intermediaries that the Ukrainian president would not be targeted.The latest claims, however, have not been independently verified, and neither the Kremlin nor Russian officials have publicly confirmed a decision to authorise attacks on Ukraine's political leadership.You use AI every day. articles.title: Faith, pollution and politics: How Yamuna takes centre stage every Chhath Puja
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Purity, hygiene and cleanliness are paramount for devotees during Chhath Puja.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Purity, hygiene and cleanliness are paramount for devotees during Chhath Puja. With God as their witness - quite literally in this case - devotees go to great lengths to observe strict hygiene while following elaborate rituals centred around the worship of the Sun deity over four days.In Delhi, however, devotees will step into the sullied waters of the Yamuna, believing that their faith will protect them.As Delhi is already gasping for breath after Diwali, the debate has now pivoted to the pollution of the river which Delhi, for most of the year, views from the bridges built over it.As thousands of people come down to the Yamuna's banks, the river will undergo its annual public audit by devotees standing waist-deep in its waters.Significance of ChhathChhath Puja, rooted in devotion to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, is primarily observed by people from Bihar, eastern UP and Jharkhand.Observed over four days, the festival begins with Nahay-Khay, when devotees prepare simple, traditional food while observing strict personal hygiene and purity.This is followed by Kharna, when jaggery-based kheer and wheat rotis are prepared as prasad.After Kharna, devotees undertake a rigorous 36-hour nirjala fast, abstaining from both food and water. The rituals culminate in offerings of arghya to the setting Sun, followed by prayers to the rising Sun on the final day.Chhath and politics go hand in hand in DelhiEvery year, as Chhath Puja approaches, the Yamuna becomes more than a river for Delhi.This year, BJP MP Manoj Tiwari took a dip in the Yamuna at Sonia Vihar, praising the cleanup under chief minister Rekha Gupta.“How can we not appreciate the work that has been done here?” he said. “There might be crocodiles in the water here, but crocodiles come in clean water.”AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar answered by floating an effigy of Tiwari at Kalindi Kunj and challenging him to bathe there, claiming that stretch was far more polluted.On Nahay Khay, the first day of the festival, a video purportedly showing dead fish near Sonia Vihar surfaced on social media.Delhi ministers accused AAP of staging it, alleging that party workers bought fish from the market and dumped them in the river.Delhi AAP chief Saurabh Bharadwaj denied this and demanded an inquiry on Friday, saying water samples had not yet been collected to establish the cause.The river has been a political flashpoint around Chhath before. Last year, AAP alleged that a temporary artificial pool at Vasudev Ghat was built to project a clean Yamuna ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s planned Chhath visit, which did not take place.Why Chhath has become a political eventChhath's growing political importance has a lot to do with Delhi's changing demography. According to reports, continued migration from Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern UP has increased the share of the Purvanchali community to about 30 percent of Delhi's population.The festival offers political parties an opportunity to reach a sizeable constituency through a celebration deeply woven into its cultural identity.According to reports, the Delhi government is setting up 1,482 Chhath ghats across 996 locations. The growing prominence of a festival once largely observed within community networks reflects how it has become an important fixture on the capital's political calendar.Why the Yamuna turns frothy around ChhathThe Yamuna's pollution becomes particularly visible around Chhath Puja, when devotees gather in large numbers along its banks to offer prayers.While talking to the Times of India, environmentalist Saumya Dutta said that the timing of Chhath coincides with a period when the river's flow has receded considerably after the monsoon, leaving less water to dilute the pollutants entering it.“During the days of Chhath Puja, tens of thousands of Delhi residents from Bihar and eastern UP, along with others, add huge amounts of pollutants, particularly detergents containing surfactants, which are common ingredients in soaps and detergents, as well as some industrial waste,” Dutta said.“Long after the peak monsoon flow, this is the period when the Yamuna's flow becomes very low. This low water flow, combined with high amounts of surfactants, causes large amounts of foam when the water is agitated. This becomes particularly visible during the huge influx of people and pollutants into this short 2% stretch of the Yamuna,” he said.According to Dutta, the 22-km stretch through the capital accounts for roughly 2% of the Yamuna's total length but contributes 70-80% of its overall pollution load.“Defaming agents and pre-Chhath cleaning do help for a very short period, but as the incoming pollution does not go down, this benefit is very short-term and vanishes quickly,” Dutta told TOI.“The major reason for the abject failure of Yamuna cleaning plans, as well as schemes like Namami Gange, is that the huge daily inflow of partially treated or even untreated sewage and industrial effluent into the river is not being tackled,” he added.The health risks for the devoteesIn one of the most polluted major rivers of India, devotees will stand waist-deep, waiting for the Sun to set and rise the following day.But is it safe for a person to come in contact with such polluted river?According to Dr Srijan Garg immersion during Chhath can expose people to harmful bacteria, viruses and parasites through the skin, eyes, nose and ears, and sometimes through accidental ingestion."Devotees are exposed through the skin, eyes, nose, ear and sometimes by ingestion. However, the major exposure is through the skin and can cause various infections such as folliculitis, dermatitis, fungal infections," Dr. Garg told TOI.The water is full of untreated sewage water. so swallowing that water will affect the health of the individual. Some acute infections typhoid, hepatitis A or E, giardiasis, cholera. These usually present with diarrhoea, vomiting and pain abdomen," he added.Meanwhile, Dr. Ishan Singh said that people with cuts or open wounds are particularly vulnerable to infections."Industrial discharge may introduce heavy metals such as lead, mercury, arsenic and cadmium into river water. Depending on concentration and duration of exposure, these can affect the kidneys, liver and nervous system. Some chemicals may also irritate the skin and eyes," Dr. Singh told TOI."However, their actual presence and concentration at individual ghats must be confirmed through laboratory testing. A single brief exposure should not automatically be considered a cause of heavy-metal poisoning," he added.He also said that children, pregnant women, elderly people, diabetic patients and people with weakened immunity need particular attention.Dr. Singh also advised devotees to avoid swallowing river water, keep immersion time short and stay away from areas close to sewage discharge points. Those with open wounds should preferably avoid entering the water. After immersion, devotees should wash thoroughly with clean water and soap and change out of wet clothes.Chhath will end with prayers to the rising Sun, as devotees complete the four-day rituals with hopes and gratitude. However, the Yamuna's problems will remain long after the devotees leave the ghats.The wait for a cleaner river is likely to continue, with sewage and industrial waste flowing into it despite periodic cleaning drives and political promises.And when Chhath returns next year, the river will once again face its annual public audit, with the same questions over its cleanliness and safety likely to resurface.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Lower rents, higher salaries’: Tens of thousands protest across Portugal over soaring housing costs
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across more than 30 cities and towns in Portugal on Saturday in the largest demonstration yet against
articles.body: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across more than 30 cities and towns in Portugal on Saturday in the largest demonstration yet against rising housing costs, with protesters demanding more affordable homes, limits on rent increases and stronger protection for tenants.The protests, which drew participants ranging from teenagers to retirees, reflected growing anger over housing prices that have risen much faster than incomes over the past decade.Demonstrators marched under the slogan “We won’t let them steal our right to housing”, while protesters in Lisbon chanted: “Lower rents, higher salaries”, according to news agency AFP.The demonstrations followed weeks of protests over the housing crisis, including tent camps set up in central squares in Lisbon and Porto, the country's two largest cities.Police have forcibly cleared some of these camps, with riot police and dogs deployed during certain demonstrations, drawing accusations of heavy-handed tactics.The protest movement gained momentum after parliament adopted a bill aimed at speeding up procedures for property owners to evict tenants.Demonstrators have also drawn inspiration from similar housing protests in neighbouring Spain that began last month.Housing prices outpace incomesOfficial figures underline the scale of the affordability challenge. Portugal recorded the European Union's biggest increase in the ratio of house prices to incomes between 2015 and 2025, with a rise of 61%, according to Eurostat data.The increase was 60.8%, compared with 34.3% in the Netherlands, which ranked second.Housing prices continued to climb in the more recent period. Between the first quarter of 2025 and the first quarter of 2026, prices rose by almost 20%, according to Portugal's National Statistics Institute.Rental costs have also increased sharply, rising 68% since 2020, according to the Portuguese government.The problem has been particularly pronounced in Lisbon and Porto. Factors contributing to the rise include increased demand from foreign buyers, investment funds, digital nomads and retirees, as well as the growth of tourism and the conversion of city-centre apartments into short-term accommodation.Lagging housing construction has also added to the pressure.Protesters demand rent controls and tenant protectionActivists are calling for limits on rent increases, stronger legal safeguards against evictions, more public and affordable housing, and measures to curb speculation in the property market.Susana Pacheco, a 35-year-old data analyst who works part-time as an astrologer to help pay her mortgage, said she was concerned about whether younger people would be able to afford homes of their own.“I’m really worried about young people,” Pacheco said. “I don’t know how they’re going to be able to pay” for their own home.“Things have become intolerable,” said Ana Encarnação, 42, pointing to rising living costs and the widening gap between rich and poor.Speaking to AFP, 20-year-old arts student Matile Cunha said finding decent accommodation had become difficult for students.“We just want a place where we can study, but you can't find decent accommodation,” she said. “Prices are at a level that no-one can afford.”Maite Chaves, a 40-year-old Uruguayan who has lived in Lisbon for 17 years, said: “With the little we earn and the prices of rent, we are the most unequal country in Europe.”Government promises new homesThe Portuguese government has introduced measures including tax cuts for new construction, restrictions on short-term rentals and a pledge to build 145,000 homes. However, it has acknowledged that the measures will take time to produce results.President António José Seguro, whose position is largely ceremonial but carries political influence, convened the Council of State, an advisory body, earlier this month to discuss the protests.He also met some of the demonstrators on Friday.The housing demonstrations began last month as frustration grew over years of rising costs and incomes that have failed to keep pace.You use AI every day. articles.title: Committed to ensure all inconsistencies in voter lists are addressed: EC to SC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission (EC) has told the Supreme Court that it remains committed to ensuring that all eligible voters find their names in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission (EC) has told the Supreme Court that it remains committed to ensuring that all eligible voters find their names in electoral rolls while simultaneously addressing inconsistencies in the lists during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise."There have been and will be problems that arise from time to time and the Commission remains alive to the need to ensure that those who are eligible to vote find their names in the voters' lists but equally, at the same time, to ensure that all inconsistencies in these lists are addressed," the poll panel said in an affidavit filed before the Supreme Court, as reported by news agency PTI.The EC said voters whose names were missing from the draft electoral rolls despite being enrolled in previous electoral rolls could apply afresh using Form 6 without facing prosecution, provided they were not already registered in another parliamentary or assembly constituency and their declarations complied with the law.The clarification came after concerns were raised that such applicants could face prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, for submitting Form 6 despite having been registered earlier. The Commission said it had asked chief electoral officers to publicise the clarification widely, including in local languages.According to PTI, the EC also informed the court that it had taken note of its suggestion to reach out to voters categorised as ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate) to facilitate their inclusion in electoral rolls.In a communication dated November 6, 2026, the Commission directed chief electoral officers in states and Union territories where the SIR is underway to allow voters to submit duly filled Enumeration Forms to the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) or Booth Level Officer (BLO) at their current ordinary residence.Voters who have not shifted can submit a signed Enumeration Form along with a statement explaining why they had not submitted it earlier. The documents can be submitted personally or through family members. An online submission facility with e-sign is also available on ECINET.The EC said it had directed the creation of a mechanism to ensure that no eligible elector was deprived of an opportunity to have their name included in the final electoral roll, while also preventing duplicate registrations.The Commission said the exercise involved challenges because of the large number of voters and the digitalisation of electoral data. It maintained that ensuring the purity of the electoral process and protecting the voting rights of eligible citizens remained its constitutional responsibility.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘These tricks don’t work on me’: Eisenkot rejects Netanyahu’s 'unity government' appeal
articles.summary: Israel's caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday renewed his call for a national unity government with political rival Gadi Eisenkot, who
articles.body: Israel's caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday renewed his call for a national unity government with political rival Gadi Eisenkot, who dismissed the appeal as a political “trick” and accused him of trying to sow division.The exchange comes as Eisenkot negotiates to form a government after being tasked with the job on Sunday. He has 28 days to form a coalition, with a possible 14-day extension.In a video statement, Netanyahu said a meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday had reinforced his belief that a unity government was necessary to protect Israel's security.Such an administration, he said, could "eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all", AFP reported.Netanyahu said the proposed government should comprise parties that recognise Israel "as a state for the Jewish people". He identified Iran as a key security concern, claiming it would "not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us".He also warned against Eisenkot's proposal to establish a minority government under the banner of a "national emergency government".Under the plan, the 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot's bloc would back the government, while Netanyahu's 46 supporters would oppose it. The remaining 26 lawmakers from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties could abstain, allowing the government to secure approval in the 120-member Knesset without an absolute majority."Instead of trying to form a weak and dangerous government... let's meet in one room, without preconditions, put aside all our disagreements and all the boycotts, and reach agreements for the security and the future of the state," Netanyahu said.Eisenkot then responded, accusing Netanyahu of making a tactical appeal despite knowing that he had lost the election."Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway; he claims to want unity but... sows division and stokes tensions as if there were no tomorrow," Eisenkot said, adding that "these tricks don't work on me", AFP reported. 'Break with extremists’ to participate in alliance: EisenkotEisenkot has indicated that he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu's Likud party and outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich's Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity was "sincere".However, an arrangement involving Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot criticised the caretaker prime minister's campaign against Arab parties as "racist".On Saturday, Eisenkot reiterated his demand for a "break with the extremists", particularly supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben Gvir, as a condition for their participation in any government led by him.According to AFP, the two sides are also at odds over the election of the Knesset speaker, scheduled for Tuesday. The post is currently held by Amir Ohana, a close Netanyahu ally. The opposition has nominated Matan Kahana, a former Israeli army officer who was fifth on Eisenkot's electoral list, to replace him."If they (Likud and its allies) are truly seeking a sincere political partnership, as they claim, they must allow the democratic process to unfold normally... and instruct their members of parliament to support the appointment of Matan Kahana," Eisenkot said.Coalition negotiations are expected to be difficult, particularly amid Netanyahu's campaign against Arab-Israeli parties, which secured a record number of seats in the election. His proposed unity government would include major Jewish parties from the centre to the right, while excluding Arab parties.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Liquor is Noida's problem; in Gurgaon and Delhi, it's obesity
articles.summary: Nearly four in every 10 men aged 15 and above in Noida use tobacco, the highest among four NCR cities, including Delhi, Gurgaon and Ghaziabad, the latest
articles.body: Nearly four in every 10 men aged 15 and above in Noida use tobacco, the highest among four NCR cities, including Delhi, Gurgaon and Ghaziabad, the latest National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6) has found.According to NFHS-6 (2023-24), tobacco use among men in Noida increased from 29.7% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 38.7%, a jump of nine percentage points. Noida also recorded a rise in alcohol consumption from 17.3% to 21.8%, the sharpest increase among the four cities, in the corresponding period.In Ghaziabad, tobacco use among men rose from 22.3% to 28.4% and alcohol consumption from 13.4% to 16.9% during the period.In contrast, Delhi saw a decline in tobacco use among men during the period from 26.2% to 21.3%. Alcohol consumption also went down from 21.6% to 16.1%. Gurgaon also recorded a substantial decline in tobacco use, from 32.6% to 23.7%, although alcohol consumption increased marginally from 18.5% to 19.9%.The survey revealed that the number of women consuming tobacco in Ghaziabad nearly doubled from 1.7% to 3.3% in the three years.The numbers fell in all three other cities - Noida recorded a decline from 3% to 2.3%, Gurgaon from 2.9% to 2.3%, and Delhi from 2.2% to 1.7%.Gurgaon recorded a sharp 17.6 percentage-point jump in overweight and obesity among women. The data show that the number of women in the 15 to 49 years age bracket with a body mass index (BMI) of 25 or above went up from 24.3% to 41.9% during the period. Delhi also recorded a marginal increase, from 41.4% to 42.7%.In contrast, Noida and Ghaziabad recorded declines in overweight and obesity among women. In Noida, the number of women with obesity fell from 34.7% to 30.2%, and in Ghaziabad it came down to 38.7% from 43.7%.However, the decline in overweight and obesity numbers was accompanied by an increase in underweight prevalence among women in all four cities. In Ghaziabad, the proportion of women with a BMI below 18.5 rose from 11.1% to 16%, while Noida recorded a marginal increase from 15% to 16%. Gurgaon also recorded a rise in underweight women, from 9% to 14.1%, while Delhi's figure increased from 10% to 12.4%.A BMI of 18.5-24.9 kg/m² is considered normal or healthy. A BMI below 18.5 is classified as underweight, 25-29.9 as overweight, and 30 or above as obese.The report also revealed contrasting trends in diabetes management across NCR. In Delhi, the number of men aged 15 and above with high or very high random blood sugar levels, or taking medication to control blood sugar, increased sharply from 14.1% to 22.2%. Among women, it rose from 12.2% to 19%.Ghaziabad recorded a sharper incidence among women, from 17.9% to 21.6%, compared with an increase from 20.2% to 20.8% among men. In Gurgaon, the proportion of men with high or very high random blood sugar levels, or taking medication to control blood sugar spikes, rose from 15.4% to 17.2%, while that among women dipped marginally from 13.5% to 13%.Noida was the only city where the high blood sugar indicators declined for both sexes. The prevalence among men fell from 17.2% to 13.6%, while among women it declined from 14.8% to 12.3%.The indicator includes adults with random blood sugar above 140 mg/dl or those taking medication to control it, and does not necessarily represent confirmed diabetes diagnoses.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Noida | Silver Rate in Noida | Bank Holidays in Noida | Public Holidays in Noida | Noida AQI | Weather in Noida | Petrol Price in Noida | Diesel Price in Noida | CNG Price in Noida | LPG Price in NoidaStay updated with the latest Noida news. articles.title: Pennsylvania plans to turn an underperforming gas well into a geothermal power source, targeting 1 megawatt of electricity and heat for nearby communities through a $14 million pilot
articles.summary: Pennsylvania will test whether an underperforming natural gas well can generate electricity and provide heat to nearby communities.
articles.body: Pennsylvania will test whether an underperforming natural gas well can generate electricity and provide heat to nearby communities. The pilot project will use geothermal energy drawn from deep underground in Indiana County, where a well will be adapted to bring heated water to the surface.The goal is to generate one megawatt of electricity for the local grid, while supplying heat to homes and businesses. Lehigh University is part of the team working on the project, led by the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection and funded by the US Department of Energy. According to Lehigh University, the project has a budget of about $14 million and will examine whether existing energy infrastructure can serve a new purpose in Pennsylvania communities.How is Pennsylvania turning an old gas well into a geothermal energy sourceThe pilot will use a deep existing unconventional gas well in Indiana County, Pennsylvania, where the geology is considered favourable for accessing geothermal resources. The well is operated by CNX Green Ventures, an Appalachian oil and gas producer. The team plans to draw heat from the existing gas well by circulating water at depth.The heated water will then be brought to the surface. Its energy is intended to generate electricity for the local grid and provide direct-use heat to nearby homes and businesses. The project’s target is one megawatt of electricity. Researchers will test whether this approach can make use of infrastructure already built by the state’s energy industry in Pennsylvania communities.Lehigh University secures $1.6 million for Pennsylvania geothermal energy pilotLehigh University has received $1.6 million to take part in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania EGS Pilot Demonstration. EGS stands for ‘enhanced geothermal system’. The wider project has a total budget of about $14 million and is funded by the US Department of Energy. Pennsylvania’s Department of Environmental Protection is leading the work in coordination with the Pennsylvania Geological Survey.Other partners include Gradient Geothermal Inc., Teverra Inc., Idaho National Laboratory, CNX Green Ventures and Seequent. Lehigh’s funding will support researchers and students from its Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences and Energy Research Center. The university’s team includes faculty members Frank Pazzaglia, Steve Peters, Anne Meltzer, Carlos Romero and Muhannad Suleiman.What makes Pennsylvania’s old gas wells valuable for geothermal energyThe project will examine whether existing oil and gas infrastructure can be used as a source of clean, renewable energy. Frank Pazzaglia, the project’s principal investigator and a professor of Earth and environmental sciences at Lehigh, said, “Pennsylvania’s conventional hydrocarbon industry, followed by the shale oil and gas revolution left behind a vast network of wells and related infrastructure.”“This project asks whether we can give that infrastructure a second life as a clean, renewable energy source.”Carlos Romero, a Lehigh professor of mechanical engineering and mechanics and director of Lehigh’s Energy Research Center, said, “Repurposing abandoned hydrocarbon wells for low-enthalpy geothermal mining represents an economic and environmental opportunity, transforming the methane-leaking liability into a predictable source of clean, local energy.”Pennsylvania project explores new roles for oil and gas workersProject leaders say the approach could create opportunities for workers displaced from the oil, gas, and coal industries. Their experience working underground could transfer directly to the geothermal sector. By extending the useful life of existing wells, the project aims to encourage geothermal energy development, particularly in the eastern United States.Geothermal resources are more restricted in that region than in the western United States. The team also wants to demonstrate that the approach can be used in other locations. The project will involve scientists and engineers from different disciplines, alongside researchers and students.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘Utterly ridiculous take’: US official rejects report claiming Quad is on ‘life support’ under Trump
articles.summary: The United States has rejected a media report claiming that the Quad alliance involving India, the US, Australia and Japan is faltering under Trump
articles.body: The United States has rejected a media report claiming that the Quad alliance involving India, the US, Australia and Japan is faltering under Trump administration, with a senior State Department official calling the assessment "utterly ridiculous".US assistant secretary of state for global public affairs Dylan Johnson pushed back against the November 14 report by Politico, which suggested that the strategic grouping had been left "on life support" because of the Trump administration's policy approach and what it described as a lack of engagement.In a post on X, Johnson cited regular diplomatic engagements among the four countries to counter the report."This is an utterly ridiculous take. @SecRubio has formally met with the Quad foreign ministers five times in the past two years — with three meetings in the past six months. The Secretary’s first official call in office was to the Quad. We have regular monthly Quad sherpa calls and meetings," he wrote.He added that Washington will look to formalise a Quad leaders' summit on the sidelines of the ASEAN meetings in Manila next week, describing the report as "Fake News!"The Quadrilateral Security Dialogue, or Quad, is a strategic grouping of India, the United States, Japan and Australia. It focuses on cooperation in the Indo-Pacific, including maritime security, regional stability, infrastructure, technology, health and disaster response. The grouping is not a formal military alliance.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had said last month that the four countries had agreed to hold the summit in Manila. He said the meeting would focus on delivering "concrete actions" rather than being a social gathering.However, the ministry of external affairs has not confirmed whether Prime Minister Narendra Modi will meet US President Donald Trump or whether a Quad leaders' meeting will take place during the visit.PM Modi is scheduled to travel to the Philippines from November 16 to 18 to attend the ASEAN meetings and the East Asia Summit. At a briefing, Secretary (East) Rudrendra Tandon said the programme was still being developed. "This is a programme that is quickly being developed and we don't have information as of now about it, except that the PM is attending the ASEAN meet in the Philippines," he said.A meeting between PM Modi and Trump would be their first in-person interaction since the Republican Party's setbacks in the US midterm elections. The two leaders last met at the G7 summit in France and spoke over the phone in September. Their discussions would also come amid ongoing negotiations on an India-US trade deal.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said tribal communities had suffered the most due to Naxal violence and accused previous governments of leaving them to fend for themselves.Addressing the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, virtually, PM Modi said tribal communities had always stood up against injustice.He said his government had allocated more than Rs 1 lakh crore for the development of tribal areas and made every effort to improve their lives.50 crore people out of extreme povertyThe Prime Minister also described bringing 50 crore people out of extreme poverty as one of India's biggest achievements since Independence.In his address, he said Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, celebrated every year on November 15 since 2021 to mark the birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Bhagwan Birsa Munda, had now become a national celebration."There was a time when several festivals and occasions were decided from a foreign point of view. articles.title: Endangered colourful San Francisco garter snakes released into the wild for the first time as 62 zoo-born youngsters begin life in California’s San Mateo County
articles.summary: Endangered San Francisco garter snakes have been released into the wild for the first time, a milestone for conservation in California.
articles.body: Endangered San Francisco garter snakes have been released into the wild for the first time, a milestone for conservation in California. Sixty-two young snakes born at the San Francisco Zoo were set free at carefully chosen sites across San Mateo County, one of only two California counties where the species lives naturally, earlier this autumn. The reptile has featured on the United States endangered species list since its first edition in 1967, which makes this captive-bred release a significant turning point for the species. Wildlife managers hope the achievement clears the way for further releases of the same kind. The zoo said the release marks a major milestone in a decades-long effort to bring the species back from the brink of extinction.Biologists see the first release as a step toward healthy populations that can sustain themselvesAccording to Popular Science, the successful rewilding of dozens of the endangered snakes is a huge moment for population rehabilitation efforts. Karine Tokatlian, a biologist at the Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District, said in a statement that the snakes’ return represents years of research, collaboration, habitat restoration and careful conservation work. She described the first release as an important step toward healthy, resilient populations that can sustain themselves over the long term. The San Francisco Zoo said the project brought together multiple agencies and organisations, combining scientific research, habitat protection and restoration with hands-on animal care to support the species’ recovery.Researchers estimate only a few thousand harmless, brightly coloured snakes remain in the wildThe species has endured nearly six decades of droughts, invasive species, disease, low genetic diversity and poaching. The snake is slender but can grow anywhere from 18 to 55 inches long, roughly 46 to 140 centimetres. Its eyes are larger than those of most garter snakes, which allows it to stay active during daylight hours. With no fangs and only mildly toxic saliva, it is essentially harmless to humans, although its bites are fatal to prey such as smaller reptiles and rodents. The San Francisco Zoo said only a couple thousand individuals are estimated to remain in the wild. The species is found only in San Mateo County and a small portion of Santa Cruz County, and nowhere else on Earth.Genetic testing at the zoo decided where each head-started snake would be releasedHead-starting is the process of rearing young animals in captivity before releasing them, which protects creatures during the most vulnerable stage of their lives. For these snakes it began in 2025, when conservationists collected several pregnant females from a healthy preserve in California’s Midpeninsula. Researchers released the adults back into their habitat after they gave birth and kept the infants at the San Francisco Zoo. After testing each snake’s genetics, conservationists placed about one-third in the same area as their mothers. The other two-thirds went to sites that particularly needed a bigger genetic pool for breeding. The zoo said the young snakes were raised until they reached a size better able to withstand threats such as predation and competition for prey. Release locations have not been disclosed to protect the snakes from illegal collection, vehicle mortality and disease.Another generation of more than 130 snakes born at the zoo this year is waiting for release in 2027Biologists continue to monitor the first head-started generation, and the next batch is still being raised at the zoo. More than 130 additional San Francisco garter snake babies were born there in 2026 and are being prepared for another round of releases planned for 2027. Post-release monitoring will help researchers determine how effectively the two rounds of releases improve populations at their sites and what lessons can be applied to future head-starting efforts. Ariel Starr, a wildlife ecologist at the same district, added that the species’ critical status is not unique. She said the project’s success and research should hopefully inform the recovery of many other imperilled reptile species.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: UP horror: 3 siblings returning from Haryana killed as pickup hits bike, brick-laden tractor runs them over amid dense fog
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: An 18-year-old teenager and his two sisters, aged 18 and 19, were killed after their motorcycle was hit by a speeding pickup vehicle and
articles.body: LUCKNOW: An 18-year-old teenager and his two sisters, aged 18 and 19, were killed after their motorcycle was hit by a speeding pickup vehicle and subsequently run over by an overloaded, brick-laden tractor-trailer amid poor visibility in Sitapur district early Sunday morning.The accident occurred around 6am near a petrol pump in the Rihar area under the Tambaur police station limits.Dense fog and low visibility reportedly reduced visibility on the road, leaving little room for the victims to escape the impact of the collision. All three died on the spot.The deceased were identified as Shishupal, 18, son of Tuka Ram, and his sisters Pooja Devi, 19, and Gayatri Devi, 18. All three belonged to Devpalpur village in the Tambaur area of Sitapur.According to information, the siblings had gone to Haryana to work as labourers and returned to Laharpur late Saturday night.Two residents of their village had reportedly reached Laharpur on separate motorcycles to receive them. On Sunday morning, Shishupal took both his sisters on his motorcycle and set off for their native village.However, when they reached near a petrol pump in Rihar, a speeding pickup allegedly rammed into their motorcycle amid the poor visibility.The impact threw all three onto the road. Before they could move to safety, an overloaded tractor-trailer carrying bricks ran over them, leaving them with fatal injuries.According to local residents, none of the three siblings was wearing a helmet at the time of the accident.The incident triggered panic in the area, with residents gathering at the spot after seeing the bodies lying on the road. The police were alerted and reached the scene shortly afterwards.The police took custody of the bodies and sent them for post-mortem examinations to complete the necessary legal formalities.Tambaur station house officer Pradeep Singh said the police were searching for the tractor-trailer and its driver.Further action would be taken after tracing the vehicle and establishing the circumstances leading to the accident.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: A New York co-op says a woman’s shower has leaked into the flat below, but she disputes it after about 10 inspections; the building is seeking nearly $170,000 in legal fees as a three-year dispute continues
articles.summary: A disagreement over a possible bathroom leak has turned into a costly legal battle between a New York homeowner and her co-operative apartment building,
articles.body: A disagreement over a possible bathroom leak has turned into a costly legal battle between a New York homeowner and her co-operative apartment building, with the dispute now involving nearly $170,000 in legal fees. Guillermina Girardi, a resident of Manhattan’s Castle Village complex, maintains that her shower is not responsible for water damage reported in the apartment below. The building, however, insists that repairs are necessary. The case, reported by the New York Post and examined through decisions published by the New York State Unified Court System, has also raised questions about the authority of co-operative housing boards and the evidence required to establish responsibility for property damage. The dispute began in 2023, approximately six weeks after Girardi purchased her one-bedroom apartment for $660,000. Her downstairs neighbour, Ariane Zorgniotti, reported signs of moisture damage on her bathroom ceiling, including peeling and bubbling paint. Building management initially treated the problem as a relatively minor leak before later describing the situation as more serious.Castle Village eventually attributed the suspected leak to a possible defect in Girardi’s shower pan, the waterproof base beneath the shower floor. The building sought permission to enter her apartment and replace the shower installation, arguing that the responsibility for the repairs rested with the apartment owner under the co-operative’s rules. Girardi challenged the diagnosis, pointing to multiple inspections by New York City housing authorities that did not establish a leak originating from her apartment. According to the court records, inspections conducted by the city’s Department of Housing Preservation and Development in 2024 did not identify a cracked shower pan or confirm a leak in the downstairs bathroom. One violation was issued over peeling plaster and paint.The legal proceedings have produced different assessments of the available evidence. In March 2025, a New York Supreme Court judge found that the building had not provided sufficient evidence at that stage to establish the source of the alleged leak. The judge modified an earlier order, removing the requirement that Girardi allow immediate repair work while retaining the building’s right to inspect her bathroom.In June 2025, the same court declined to grant summary judgment to either side, finding that questions about whether a leak existed remained unresolved. The judge noted that the housing department’s inspection reports supported Girardi’s position, while the building had submitted statements from its staff and the downstairs resident, along with photographs of the reported damage.However, the legal position shifted in March 2026. New York’s Appellate Division, First Department, overturned the lower court’s decision and ruled in favour of Castle Village. The appellate court found that the building had presented sufficient initial evidence of a leak through photographs and sworn statements from its assistant superintendent and the downstairs resident. It directed Girardi to provide access for repairs at her expense under the terms of her proprietary lease. The court also rejected her argument that the building had deliberately singled her out for unfair treatment.The proposed work would involve removing her existing shower and replacing parts of the bathroom with standard building materials. The original estimate was approximately $9,200, although Girardi believes the actual cost could reach $40,000, particularly because the renovation would involve replacing the existing Carrara marble tiles.The conflict has also been complicated by an earlier disagreement over a building-wide gas-pipe replacement project. Girardi had objected to the proposed placement of a horizontal pipe across her kitchen ceiling, arguing that it would interfere with plans to create a private home office. The building subsequently took legal action to obtain access for the installation, and she eventually complied with the arrangement.Meanwhile, the financial consequences of the ongoing dispute have continued to grow. Castle Village is now seeking nearly $170,000 from Girardi in legal fees, adding another substantial expense to a disagreement that began with reports of water damage. The latest development came when a building contractor arrived at Girardi’s apartment intending to carry out the proposed bathroom work. She sought the contractor’s plumbing licence details and the necessary permit from the city’s Department of Buildings, but the information was not provided, according to the recorded interaction described in the New York Post report.Despite the appellate ruling, the disagreement over the proposed work, its cost and the legal fees has continued, turning what initially appeared to be a routine maintenance issue into a prolonged dispute between a homeowner and her co-operative building.You use AI every day. articles.title: Birsa Munda Jayanti 2026: date, history, significance, and all you need to know
articles.summary: Stories of freedom fighters inspire generations of people with their brave contributions to the country’s freedom struggle.
articles.body: Stories of freedom fighters inspire generations of people with their brave contributions to the country’s freedom struggle. One such freedom fighter from India is Birsa Munda, who died quite young but left an indelible mark on the nation’s history.Birsa Munda Jayanti, celebrated in November every year, marks the birth anniversary of a freedom fighter and social reformer who is lovingly called "Dharti Aba," or "Father of the Earth." He stood up bravely against British exploitation and worked to protect the land, culture, and rights of his people.The day is more than a tribute to the past. It celebrates tribal pride, identity, and empowerment across the country.Here is the history and significance of Birsa Munda Jayanti is celebrated every yearBirsa Munda Jayanti 2026: date, history and significanceBirsa Munda Jayanti is celebrated on 15 November each year. This year marks his 151st birth anniversary, last year was his 150th and was marked as Janjatiya Gaurav Varsh for that milestone.Who was Birsa Munda?Birsa Munda was born on 15 November 1875 in Ulihatu village, in present-day Khunti district of Jharkhand. His birth name was Daud Munda and he belonged to the Munda tribe of the Chotanagpur Plateau. His childhood was shaped by the growing hardships Adivasi communities faced under British rule. His followers called him "Dharti Aba," or "Father of the Earth." He later emerged as a tribal leader, social reformer, religious preacher and anti-colonial freedom fighter.The Ulgulan: a revolt against injusticeBirsa's most important well-known chapter is the Ulgulan of 1899–1900, meaning the "Great Tumult," and was centred on the Chotanagpur Plateau, a major tribal uprising against British rule, challenging exploitative land settlements and forest laws. At its heart was a simple demand: protect the traditional land rights of the Mundas and push back against outside exploitation.The British eventually caught him in around February/ March 1900 at Jamkopai forest, followed by this, he died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900. Even though the official cause was cholera, foul play was suspected passing away at the tender age of 24 or 25.What changed after his deathHis struggle did not end with him. The rebellion forced the colonial government to bring in laws so tribal land could not be easily taken over by outsiders, known as dikus, which led to the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act of 1908. A century later, another milestone arrived when the state of Jharkhand, meaning "land of forests," officially came into existence on 15 November 2000, which was Birsa's birth anniversary.How Janjatiya Gaurav Divas beganSince 2021, 15 November has had a second name. The Union Cabinet met on 10 November 2021 and named the day Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, to remember tribal freedom fighters as part of the 75th anniversary of independence. The day exists to honour tribal freedom fighters and celebrate India's rich tribal heritage.Why is Birsa Munda Jayanti celebrated?Birsa Munda Jayanti honours the memory of Birsa Munda, one of India’s most influential tribal freedom fighters and social reformers.Here is why the day is important.A tribute to a brave freedom fighterBirsa led the Ulgulan against British colonial policies. His revolt stood up against unfair land laws that were hurting Adivasi communities.A celebration of tribal identity and cultureHe brought the Munda, Oraon and other tribes together to resist the suppression of their way of life. The day honours the rich heritage, traditions and values of India’s tribal communities.Recognition of his fight for landBirsa opposed the British zamindari system, which pushed tribal families off their ancestral land. His struggle later led to reforms that protected tribal land ownership.An inspiration for social changeHe urged people to give up superstitions and exploitative practices. He also promoted equality and moral discipline.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: From kidneys to body tissues: Desperate Iranians put organs up for sale as war drags on, claims report
articles.summary: Iran's worsening economic crisis is pushing some residents to desperate lengths, with people offering to sell multiple organs and body tissues, including
articles.body: Iran's worsening economic crisis is pushing some residents to desperate lengths, with people offering to sell multiple organs and body tissues, including kidneys, bone marrow, testicles and corneas, to escape mounting debts and meet basic household expenses. An investigation by Iran International has found a growing online market in which financially distressed Iranians are advertising body parts for sale, with some even willing to part with vital organs to secure their families' futures.The findings come as Iran faces mounting economic pressure amid the lingering conflict in the Middle East, a US naval blockade and stringent sanctions. With little clarity over when the standoff between Tehran and Washington will ease, concerns are growing over the impact of prolonged economic uncertainty on ordinary Iranians. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has reportedly warned that the pressure could continue indefinitely, while predicting further deterioration in Iran's economy over the coming months, according to Al Jazeera.Iranians advertise organs for saleIran International examined more than 600 advertisements posted on a Telegram channel between late May and late October. Its investigation found that approximately one in three advertisements offered more than one organ or type of body tissue.Kidneys were the most frequently advertised, featuring in 498 listings. Bone marrow appeared in 279 advertisements, followed by liver in 51, testicles in 15 and corneas in two. In 142 listings, sellers offered both kidneys and bone marrow, while another 26 advertised kidneys, bone marrow and liver together.Some advertisements also raised questions about whether sellers understood the medical procedures they were proposing. One man offering several body parts, including a testicle, told Iran International: "I can still live after losing these organs." He appeared unaware that some of the procedures he was offering were not established transplant options in Iran.Interviews with prospective sellers revealed the financial desperation behind the listings. One man said he was willing to give up even vital organs to secure his young daughter's future. Another, a former clothing business owner, said bankruptcy had left him with mounting debts and bounced cheques. He hoped selling an organ would help him repay at least some of his liabilities.Others described struggling with years of renting accommodation or simply trying to afford everyday necessities. A single mother raising two daughters said she was searching for a buyer to support her family's basic expenses.US economic pressure adds to Tehran's challengesThe situation is unfolding as Washington reportedly shifts towards sustained economic pressure on Tehran after months of fighting and negotiations.According to Al Jazeera, Rubio told G7 counterparts in Paris that a naval blockade, stringent sanctions and disruptions to overland trade could remain in place without a clear end date.Tehran-based economist Isaac Saidian warned that if the economic siege pushes Iran's oil revenues close to zero, the government could face one of the most difficult periods in its recent history. The challenge, he said, would extend beyond foreign currency shortages to paying salaries and pensions, supplying essential goods and preventing further inflation.President Masoud Pezeshkian's administration has prepared for the possibility of prolonged restrictions, although Iranian authorities have rejected suggestions of an impending economic collapse.Meanwhile, military tensions remain a concern. The IRGC has claimed responsibility for drone attacks targeting a US air defence radar installation in Bahrain, while Iranian forces have also reported oil tankers catching fire after striking naval mines around the Strait of Hormuz.You use AI every day. articles.title: After their father died without a will in 2021, two Indiana half-siblings fought over property in Indiana and California; a November 13 appeals court upheld $177,852 in sanctions against the brother over a settlement
articles.summary: When a parent dies without leaving a will, disputes among family members can become complicated, particularly when an estate includes property in
articles.body: When a parent dies without leaving a will, disputes among family members can become complicated, particularly when an estate includes property in different states. In Indiana, two half-siblings became involved in a prolonged legal battle over their late father's estate, including real estate in Indiana and California. Although they eventually reached a mediated settlement, disagreements over its terms led to further court proceedings and a substantial financial penalty for the brother.In a November 13, 2026 opinion, the Indiana Court of Appeals upheld sanctions of $177,852.86 against Michael W Clark. The ruling in Michael Clark v. Elisa Mrozinski, available on Justia, found no abuse of discretion in the trial court's decision to penalise him for violating a settlement agreement and an earlier court order.Dispute began after father's deathAccording to the court's opinion, Clark and Elisa Mrozinski were half-siblings and children of James L. Clark, who died without a will on September 8, 2021. Mrozinski had previously served as her father's power of attorney and was appointed personal representative of his estate after his death.Clark filed a legal action in September 2021 seeking an accounting of Mrozinski's actions while acting as his father's power of attorney. An estate case was also opened in Indiana, while separate proceedings were initiated in California to handle property located there.The dispute later expanded to include TransAmerican, Inc., a corporation owned by their father and managed by Mrozinski. Clark filed another action in 2023 seeking access to the company's corporate records. That case was subsequently consolidated with the existing proceedings.Siblings reached settlement over propertiesAfter several years of litigation, the siblings participated in mediation on July 9, 2024, and signed a settlement agreement. Under its terms, the estate was to transfer certain California real estate to Clark, while he agreed to purchase certain Indiana real estate from the estate.Disagreements emerged soon after the agreement was signed. Both siblings accused the other of failing to fulfil their obligations. In August 2024, they filed separate motions asking the court to enforce the settlement, with Clark alternatively requesting that it be terminated.On September 16, 2024, the trial court rejected Clark's request and directed both parties to proceed in good faith under the agreement. It clarified that disputes concerning the California property would be decided by the California court, while it retained authority over the remaining claims. Clark subsequently filed objections in the California estate proceedings, challenging aspects of the settlement and arguing that it was unenforceable.Court imposes $177,852 in sanctionsMrozinski later asked the Indiana court to hold Clark in contempt, arguing that his objections in California violated the September 2024 order and the settlement agreement. The California court rejected his objections in May 2025.In October 2025, the Indiana trial court found that Clark had knowingly and willingly violated its earlier order. It determined that his failure to comply had caused Mrozinski and the entities she represented to incur $117,655.50 in additional taxes, insurance and security expenses. The court also included $51,617.75 in attorney fees and another $8,579.61 in expenses, bringing the total to $177,852.86. After Clark filed a motion to correct error, the court amended its order in January 2026 but left the sanctions in place.Clark challenged the decision on appeal, arguing that he had not acted in bad faith and had not received sufficient notice that damages would be considered at the hearing. The appeals court rejected his arguments concerning the sanctions hearing. It found that the earlier order clearly required him to comply with the settlement and that he had sufficient notice that financial damages and attorney fees were being sought. The court also noted that Clark had not presented a sufficiently developed argument challenging the amount or type of sanctions.Appeals court upholds sanctionsOn November 13, 2026, the Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the sanctions of $177,852.86 against Clark. It also remanded the case for the trial court to consider whether Mrozinski could recover additional attorney fees incurred during the appeal. The appeals judges declined to award appellate attorney fees themselves, finding that Clark's procedural errors did not meet the required standard for such an award.The decision leaves the original sanctions intact while allowing the lower court to consider further legal costs. It highlights how disputes over family estates can continue even after relatives reach a settlement, particularly when one party challenges the agreement or fails to follow court orders.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari accuses TMC of treating only Muslims as minorities
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday accused the previous Trinamool Congress (TMC) government of considering only Muslims as a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday accused the previous Trinamool Congress (TMC) government of considering only Muslims as a minority community, asserting that Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains also qualify as religious minorities.Adhikari made the remarks during a visit to Gurdwara Bara Sikh Sangat in Burrabazar, Kolkata's trading hub. He greeted members of the Sikh community at the gurdwara and also participated in a procession organised by the community in the area, PTI reported.Addressing reporters after meeting members of the Sikh community, Adhikari said the term minority should not be associated with just one religious group. He alleged that the previous government, led by Mamata Banerjee, had failed to recognise other religious communities as minorities."Minority does not mean a particular community. Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains are also (religious) minorities. The previous TMC government considered only Muslims as a minority," the chief minister told reporters.Adhikari also praised the Sikh community, describing its members as patriots."They (Sikhs) are the truest patriots," the chief minister said.The remarks come against the backdrop of Adhikari's repeated allegations that the previous TMC government pursued a policy of appeasement towards the Muslim community to secure its electoral support. He has previously accused the Mamata Banerjee-led administration of favouring the community for political gains.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
